questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Asymptote of a Rational Function
questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{x}{2-{x}^{4}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{x}{2-{x}^{4}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{x}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}-1)} \\  & =\frac{0}{0-1} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{4{x}^{2}-9x+1}{x+4}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{4{x}^{2}-9x+1}{x+4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{4{x}^{2}}{x}-\frac{9x}{x}+\frac{1}{x})}{(\frac{x}{x}+\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x-9+\frac{1}{x})}{(1+\frac{4}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(4x-9+0)}{(1+0)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(4x)-9 \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has No Horizontal Asymptote
questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{12x-3{x}^{4}}{3{x}^{2}+7} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{3{x}^{4}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{12}{x}-3{x}^{2})}{(3+\frac{7}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{0-3{x}^{2}}{3+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(-{x}^{2}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity: Infinite Solutions
questions.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{-{x}^{6}+4{x}^{2}-2}{{x}^{5}+8} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{-{x}^{6}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{4{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{8}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(-x+\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{5}})}{(1+\frac{8}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\text{ }\frac{-x+0-0}{1+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,-x \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Horizontal Asymptote of a Rational Function
questions.problem:
The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{7}{-5{x}^{4}+3{x}^{2}-2}$ is

$y=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{7}{-5{x}^{4}+3{x}^{2}-2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{7}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{-5{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{7}{{x}^{4}})}{(-5+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{0}{-5+0-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$
